item.text: I’ll read the input and check every three-node placement against the constraints and failure scenarios.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -c 'import json,itertools
with open(\"input.json\") as f: d=json.load(f)
lat={tuple(sorted((x[\"a\"],x[\"b\"]))):x[\"ms\"] for x in d[\"latencies\"]}
valid=[]
for ns in itertools.combinations(sorted(d[\"nodes\"],key=lambda n:n[\"id\"]),3):
 ids=[n[\"id\"] for n in ns]
 cost=sum(n[\"cost\"] for n in ns)
 if cost>d[\"budget\"] or any(lat[p]>d[\"max_pair_latency\"] for p in itertools.combinations(ids,2)): continue
 weights=[]
 for s in d[\"failures\"]:
  remaining=[n for n in ns if n[\"site\"] not in s[\"sites\"] and n[\"provider\"] not in s[\"providers\"]]
  w=sum(n[\"vote_weight\"] for n in remaining)
  if w<d[\"quorum\"] or not any(n[\"writable\"] for n in remaining): break
  weights.append(w)
 else: valid.append((ids,cost,min(weights)))
best=min(valid,key=lambda x:(x[1],-x[2],x[0]))
print(json.dumps({\"feasible_placements\":sorted(x[0] for x in valid),\"selected\":best[0],\"selected_cost\":best[1],\"selected_min_surviving_weight\":best[2]}))'"
